description:
About the Position

Leiden University advertises a PhD candidate position in the research project 'Entangled with Seaweed', working on case studies in South Africa. Within the NWO Open Competition-funded programme, this line of the project studies the South African seaweed sector ethnographically: the people whose livelihoods depend on seaweed harvesting and farming, the regulatory landscape governing marine resource access, and the social and ecological entanglements that shape how the seaweed economy develops.

The doctoral candidate carries out extended fieldwork in South African coastal regions, combining interviews, participant observation and policy analysis, and collaborates closely with the Scotland-case researcher and the project's principal investigators to build a comparative account of seaweed governance and livelihoods. The position is a salaried four-year PhD employment under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement, starting at EUR 3,204 per month, with fieldwork periods in South Africa supported by project funding.

Candidate Profile and Application

Applicants hold a research master's degree in anthropology, sociology, development studies, geography or a related discipline, with strong qualitative skills and experience or clear affinity with Southern-African or maritime research contexts. Applications are made through the Leiden University careers portal with CV, transcripts, a research statement and references, and the closing date is 7 November 2026.

Highlights

  • PhD on seaweed ethnography - South Africa case studies
  • NWO Open Competition funded project
  • Comparative ethnography across two coastal regions
  • Salaried four-year position (EUR 3,204 - 4,051 per month)
  • Fieldwork supported by project funding
  • Closing date: 7 November 2026

About Leiden University

Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands and a member of the League of European Research Universities (LERU). Its seven faculties in Leiden and The Hague cover humanities, law, social and behavioural sciences, medicine, science, archaeology and governance. Doctoral candidates at Leiden are salaried employees under the CAO-NU collective agreement rather than fee-paying students, which makes its PhD positions fully funded by design. All academic vacancies, including PhD and postdoctoral roles, are advertised on the university's dedicated careers portal.
